bib.title: AGIEval: A Human-Centric Benchmark for Evaluating Foundation Models

question: How well do foundation models perform on official, human-centric standardized exams (college entrance, law, math competitions, civil service), and where do they fall short?
hypothesis: Traditional benchmarks built from artificial datasets do not represent human-level capability; exam-derived tasks give a more meaningful evaluation (implied, not framed as a testable hypothesis).
contributions: AGIEval: a bilingual (English and Chinese) benchmark of 20 tasks, 8,062 objective questions, from official high-standard admission and qualification exams
Evaluation of Text-Davinci-003, ChatGPT, GPT-4 and Vicuna-13B under zero-shot, few-shot, zero-shot CoT and few-shot CoT, compared with average and top human performance
Qualitative analysis of ChatGPT errors along understanding, knowledge, reasoning and calculation
Release of data, code and all model outputs

method.summary: Questions from Gaokao, SAT, LSAT, GRE/GMAT (via AQuA-RAT), AMC/AIME (via MATH), Chinese lawyer qualification (JEC-QA) and civil service (LogiQA) exams were filtered to objective formats (multiple-choice and fill-in-the-blank) and assembled into 20 tasks. Four LLMs were run through Azure OpenAI APIs under four prompting settings with greedy decoding, scored by accuracy or exact match, and compared with human averages. 100 wrong ChatGPT zero-shot CoT answers per task were annotated by experts.
method.task: multiple-choice and fill-in-the-blank exam question answering (language-only)

datasets.name: AGIEval (20 tasks)
datasets.split: test only; few-shot exemplars drawn from training sets or held out from the collected data
datasets.source: Gaokao and SAT from public online sources with solutions; LSAT from Wang et al. (2022) and Zhong et al. (2022), exams 1991-2016; LogiQA (Liu et al., 2021) for civil service; MATH (Hendrycks et al.) for AMC/AIME; AQuA-RAT (Ling et al., 2017) for GRE/GMAT; JEC-QA (Zhong et al., 2020) for lawyer qualification. Licence not stated.
datasets.preprocessing: Subjective questions removed, keeping only multiple-choice and fill-in-the-blank. JEC-QA (two types) and MATH down-sampled to 1,000 instances each. Language-only version released. Per-task counts: GK-geography 199, GK-biology 210, GK-history 243, GK-chemistry 207, GK-physics 200, GK-En 306, GK-Ch 246, GK-Math-QA 351, GK-Math-Cloze 118, SAT-En 206, SAT-Math 220, JEC-QA-KD 1000, JEC-QA-CA 1000, LSAT-AR 230, LSAT-LR 510, LSAT-RC 260, LogiQA-en 651, LogiQA-ch 651, AQuA-RAT 254, MATH 1000 (Table 1).

other.api: chat completion for zero-shot; completion API for few-shot

other.settings: zero-shot and zero-shot CoT only (Table 4); serving details not stated

inference.samples: one greedy generation per item; no repeated runs or seeds stated
inference.prompting: Zero-shot: '[Question] Among A to D, the answer is:'. Few-shot: 5 exemplars as 'Q: ... The answer is ...'. Zero-shot CoT: two steps (rationale generation then answer generation). Few-shot CoT: 5 exemplars with explanations, explanation and answer generated in one step. Chat API few-shot examples converted to conversation history; ChatGPT few-shot run on the completion API because it failed to follow the pattern in chat format.

parameters.few_shot_selection: random five of medium sentence length from the training set (AQuA-RAT, LogiQA, LSAT), or from collected data and excluded from test (Gaokao, SAT); first 1,000 training examples used as test set for JEC-QA with five exemplars from the rest; MATH uses the exemplars in Lewkowycz et al. (2022) appendix
parameters.cot_demonstration_sources: existing rationales for AQuA-RAT and MATH; expert annotations for Gaokao and SAT; ChatGPT-generated explanations given question and answer for LogiQA, JEC-QA, LSAT

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: standard classification accuracy on multiple-choice questions

metrics.name: Exact Match (EM)
metrics.definition: exact match on fill-in-the-blank questions (Sec 3.3.2 also names F1; Sec 4.2.3 reports EM only)

metrics.name: Human-expert capability score
metrics.definition: annotator scores 1 if the model is correct on a skill (understanding, knowledge, reasoning, calculation) and 0 otherwise, over 100 wrongly answered instances per task, ChatGPT zero-shot CoT

baselines: Top human performance (top 1%; top 10% for lawyer qualification test)
Text-Davinci-003 vs ChatGPT vs GPT-4 vs Vicuna-13B
eval.protocol: Human performance for MATH, LogiQA and JEC-QA taken from their publications; for AQuA-RAT, LSAT, SAT and Gaokao estimated by scaling average (50%) and top (1%) test-taker scores against full marks to 100. Qualitative analysis by annotators with expert knowledge (PhD students, professional researchers). No significance tests or repeated runs.

availability.data: https://github.com/ruixiangcui/AGIEval (data, code and all model outputs; CoT demonstrations also released)

results.claim: The benchmark holds 8,062 questions across 20 tasks.
results.quote: As a result, we construct a benchmark consisting of 8,062 questions for evaluation.

limits: Only objective questions (multiple choice, fill-in-the-blank) are kept; subjective and essay questions are excluded, so open-ended skill is not tested.
Language-only; multi-modal version is future work.
Human averages are estimates scaled from score distributions or taken from other papers; the authors concede they 'do not fully represent the range of skills and knowledge' of test-takers.
Data contamination cannot be ruled out: the uncontaminated check covers only six Gaokao subjects with small n (5 to 64 items), and math drops sharply on uncontaminated items.
Closed API models only (plus Vicuna-13B zero-shot); GPT-4 few-shot run through chat API only, which the authors say may be revised if a completion API appears.
Single greedy run per setting; no variance or significance testing; model versions and API dates not given.
Several Chinese-language tasks, so the results mix language and domain; LogiQA-English is a translation of the Chinese original.
CoT demonstrations for LogiQA, JEC-QA and LSAT were generated by ChatGPT.
Sec 3.3.2 names F1 for fill-in-the-blank but results use EM only; answer-extraction rules are not described.
Qualitative analysis is on 100 errors per task from ChatGPT only, with no inter-annotator agreement reported.

terms.definition: a human-centric benchmark built from official, public and high-standard admission and qualification exams for general human test-takers
two steps: the model is prompted with the question plus 'Let's think step by step' to generate an explanation, then prompted with the explanation to give the answer
